samples.summary: `height` is inside the allowlist but is effectively inert in the shipped preview, so part of the added surface delivers nothing to users. The plugin accepts `height="200"` (`img-plugin.ts:157`), yet the design doc itself records that Tailwind preflight's author-level `img { height: auto }` outranks the presentational hint the HTML dimension attribute produces, and it explicitly leaves overriding preflight "as a separate call" — there is no `img` rule in `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-preview.css` (grep for `img` there returns nothing). A note author pasting `` gets an unchanged, intrinsically sized image with no indication why, which is exactly the "renders at intrinsic size with no hint why" failure mode the plugin's decline-rather-than-drop rationale was designed to avoid. If the originating issue's acceptance mentions height sizing this is a genuine unmet criterion (major); as written it reads as accepted-but-unsupported scope, hence minor.
samples.evidence: docs/design/notes/notes.md: "Tailwind preflight ships `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto }`, and an author-CSS declaration outranks the presentational hint an HTML dimension attribute produces … Overriding preflight for preview images was left alone as a separate call."; packages/notes/src/view/img-plugin.ts: `if (height !== undefined) token.attrs.push(['height', height]);`
